column1: DAB's default JSON configuration filename is {{c1::dab-config.json}}.
column2:
Without --config, DAB looks for the standard filename. Pass --config when you want to load a different complete configuration file.
Review source

column1: DAB stores its database type and connection string in the {{c1::data-source}} section.
column2:
This section tells DAB which database provider to use and where to connect. The entities section separately determines which objects the API exposes.
Review source

column1: Global endpoint, host, and cache settings belong in DAB's {{c1::runtime}} section.
column2:
Runtime settings affect the service as a whole. For example, change the REST base path here rather than repeating it for each entity.
Review source

column1: Reference the environment variable DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING in a DAB string value with {{c1::@env('DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING')}}.
column2:
DAB reads the variable when it loads the configuration. The JSON stores the name of the variable, not its secret value. Supply the value to the running process.
Review source

column1: Configure DAB's GraphQL endpoint path with {{c1::runtime.graphql.path}}.
column2:
The path is the URL where clients submit GraphQL operations. Changing it moves the endpoint but does not change the GraphQL types that the entities expose.
Review source

column1: DAB's {{c1::runtime.host.cors.allow-credentials}} setting controls the Access-Control-Allow-Credentials response header.
column2:
The setting controls whether browsers can use credentialed cross-origin requests for allowed origins. It does not validate the credentials. DAB authentication and entity permissions still apply.
Review source

column1: Create a baseline DAB configuration for SQL Server with {{c1::dab init --database-type mssql}}.
column2:
This command creates the configuration skeleton for the SQL provider. Add entity definitions separately. Keep the connection string outside the committed file by using an environment variable reference.
Review source

column1: Add a new entity to an existing DAB configuration with {{c1::dab add}}, followed by its name, source, and permissions.
column2:
The command adds an entity to an existing configuration. The source identifies the database object, while the permission identifies who can perform an API action on it.
Review source

column1: To start DAB with the complete configuration file dab-config.production.json, run {{c1::dab start --config dab-config.production.json}}.
column2:
Use --config to point to a complete file that DAB can load. Use DAB_ENVIRONMENT when you want an environment variant to override values from a shared base.
Review source

column1: To load dab-config.Production.json as overrides for the base file, set {{c1::DAB_ENVIRONMENT}} to Production.
column2:
Use the environment value that matches your variant filename. For example, Production selects dab-config.Production.json so only its specified settings override the base.
Review source
